prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stock Ideas for the Next 12 Months

My information only runs through about May 2026, so check current prices, recent earnings, and news before buying. Most professional fund managers fail to beat the S&P 500 in any given year, and far more fail over longer periods. Treat these as researched ideas, not a guarantee.

## The List

| # | Stock | Sector | Why it could outperform | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Semiconductors | Makes nearly all of the most advanced chips for Nvidia, Apple, AMD and others, so it wins no matter which AI chip designer does. | Tension between Taiwan and China; tariffs |
| 2 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Semiconductors | Designs custom AI chips for Google, Meta and others, and sells data-center networking gear. | High valuation; depends on a few large customers |
| 3 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Communication services | Has been cheaper than its big-tech peers, with growth in Google Cloud, its own AI chips (TPUs), Gemini and Waymo. | Antitrust rulings; AI chatbots taking search traffic |
| 4 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | Consumer / cloud | AWS (its cloud business) is growing with AI demand, and its retail and advertising profits are rising. | Heavy spending on AI infrastructure; consumer slowdown |
| 5 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Industrials / energy | Sells gas turbines and power-grid equipment needed for data centers and electrification, with orders booked years ahead. | Stock has already risen a lot, so expectations are high |
| 6 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Healthcare | Leads in obesity and diabetes drugs (Zepbound, Mounjaro), and a weight-loss pill could greatly expand the market. | Drug price pressure; competition; high valuation |
| 7 | **Intuitive Surgical (ISRG)** | Healthcare | Dominates robotic surgery, and most of its revenue comes back every year from instruments and service. | Premium valuation; slower hospital spending |
| 8 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Financials | The best-run large US bank, likely to benefit from lighter regulation and more deal-making. | Recession or rising loan losses |
| 9 | **Visa (V)** | Financials | Takes a small cut of spending worldwide with very high profit margins. | Regulation of card fees; legal cases |
| 10 | **Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B)** | Diversified | A stabilizer: large cash reserves and diversified businesses help if markets fall. | Adjusting to leadership after Buffett; unlikely to lead in a strong bull market |

## Using This Well

1. **Your portfolio must differ from the index to beat it.** Several of these stocks are already large parts of the S&P 500. Holding them in equal amounts means betting on healthcare, industrials, and financials more heavily than the index does, and on Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia less heavily.
2. **About half the list depends on AI spending.** Picks 1–5 would probably all fall together if data-center spending slows. Cut that group if this concentration worries you.
3. **Consider a "core and satellite" setup.** Many investors keep 60–80% in an S&P 500 index fund and put the rest into individual picks like these. That limits how far you can fall behind while still giving you a chance to outperform.
4. **Size positions in advance.** Put roughly equal amounts in each stock (about 10% of the stock portion each), and decide now what would make you sell each one.
5. **Measure honestly.** In 12 months, compare your after-fee, after-tax return to an S&P 500 fund such as SPY or VOO over the same period, including dividends.

If you share your risk tolerance, the size of the investment, your country (which affects taxes and which brokers you can use), or sectors you want to avoid, I can tailor the list.

*This is general information, not personalized financial advice.*
